batchName: Middle Republic: The First Punic War (264-241 BCE) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Middle Republic: The First Punic War (264-241 BCE)

questions.question: How long did the First Punic War last?
questions.explanation: The war ran for 23 years, from 264 to 241 BC. It was the longest continuous conflict and the greatest naval war of the ancient world.
questions.sourceQuote: The war that ended this friendship lasted 23 years, from 264 to 241 BC.

questions.question: What did Sicily become after the First Punic War?
options: Part of the kingdom of Syracuse
questions.explanation: Sicily became Rome's first province, an overseas territory run by a Roman governor. It was also a vital source of grain.
questions.sourceQuote: Sicily became Rome's first province (*provincia*), an overseas territory run by a Roman governor, and a vital source of grain.

questions.question: What happened to Regulus, the Roman consul who invaded Africa?
options: He captured the city of Carthage
He drowned in a storm at sea
He was captured by the Carthaginians
He celebrated a triumph in Rome
questions.explanation: In 255 BC Carthage's retrained army crushed his army and Regulus was captured. He had earlier come within 16 km of Carthage by taking Tunis.
questions.sourceQuote: In 255 BC the retrained army crushed the Romans, and Regulus was captured.

questions.question: Under the Treaty of Lutatius, how much did Carthage agree to pay Rome?
questions.explanation: Carthage agreed to pay 3,200 talents of silver over ten years. It also had to leave Sicily and free all prisoners.
questions.sourceQuote: Under the Treaty of Lutatius in 241 BC, Carthage left Sicily, freed all prisoners and agreed to pay 3,200 talents of silver over ten years.

questions.question: What did the Romans call Akragas, Carthage's main base on Sicily?
questions.explanation: The Romans called the southern Sicilian port of Akragas 'Agrigentum'. A Roman army of about 40,000 besieged it in 262 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: Carthage made Akragas, a port halfway along Sicily's south coast that the Romans called Agrigentum, its main base on the island.

questions.question: In what year did the Second Punic War begin?
questions.explanation: Resentment over Rome's harsh treatment smouldered until the Second Punic War began in 218 BC. Meanwhile Hamilcar had built a new power base in Spain.
questions.sourceQuote: Resentment smouldered, and in 218 BC the Second Punic War began.

questions.question: Which consul gave Rome its first naval victory, at Mylae in 260 BC?
questions.explanation: Gaius Duilius won at Mylae against about 130 Carthaginian ships. His ravens grappled the first 30 ships, including the enemy flagship.
questions.sourceQuote: Gaius Duilius, the consul who gave Rome its first naval victory, faced about 130 Carthaginian ships.

questions.question: Which Carthaginian general took command in Sicily in 247 BC and waged a guerrilla war from the mountain of Eryx?
questions.explanation: Hamilcar Barca took command in 247 BC and tied down the Roman legions from the mountain of Eryx, near Drepana.
questions.sourceQuote: In 247 BC Hamilcar Barca, the Carthaginian general who kept up the fight in western Sicily, took command.

questions.question: Who were the Mamertines, whose call for help drew Rome into Sicily?
options: Italian mercenaries who had seized Messana
Roman allied sailors from the south
questions.explanation: The Mamertines were Italian mercenaries who seized Messana in 289 BC. Many Romans disliked the idea of aiding soldiers who had stolen a city.
questions.sourceQuote: In 289 BC Italian mercenaries called the Mamertines had seized it.

questions.question: Who is the main ancient source for the First Punic War?
questions.explanation: Almost everything known about the war comes from Polybius, a Greek taken to Rome as a hostage in 167 BC. He wrote about a century after the fighting.
questions.sourceQuote: Almost everything we know about this war comes from Polybius, a Greek taken to Rome as a hostage in 167 BC.
